findings.message: The 'anchor update' walkthrough explicitly lists its steps (verify tag -> ff-only merge -> doctor -> capability diff) but entirely omits updating dependencies (e.g., 'npm install'). If release N+1 adds a new package dependency, the collaborator's instance will crash on boot because node_modules is out of date, violating the 'works-on-arrival' criterion for updates.

Moving the status block to an engine-emitted template and explicitly removing status-request text from agent prompts eliminates the LLM's subjective self-reporting. This strips the agent of its cognitive grounding (articulating its current state, blockers, and intent before acting), replacing it with mechanical logging and severely regressing the system's core 'honesty' engineering.

findings.topic: Token leak via OS browser launcher argv
findings.message: To pass the token in a client-side URL fragment during the out-of-band bootstrap, the system must spawn the OS's browser launcher (e.g., 'start', 'open', 'xdg-open') with the target URL. This injects the token directly into the argv of that child process, violating the proposed invariant that 'the token never appears on any process argv' and ensuring the CI test will fail.

findings.topic: TOCTOU gap in skill hash verification
findings.message: The draft states skill hashes are 'verified at engine start'. If the engine dynamically reloads skill files from disk during a long-running session without re-verifying the hash at read time, a collaborator can bypass immutability by editing the file post-boot. Verification must occur at load/read time, not just boot time.
